title: Light condensed mathematics, solid abelian groups and analytic rings
summary: Light condensed sets and abelian groups; solid abelian groups and solid condensed spectra, with solidification and the solid tensor product; analytic rings with completion, colimits and localisation by idempotent algebras; smashing spectra; the solid analytic ring structures on finite-type and general discrete rings; discrete Huber pairs with descent over rational covers of their adic spectra; solid Huber rings, bounded rings, Gelfand rings and their Berkovich spectra; and the normed solid base Z((u)) with its overconvergent disc algebras. This is the algebraic foundation on which analytic stacks, ring-stack transmutation and the analytic Habiro ring are built.
readme:
# Light condensed mathematics, solid abelian groups and analytic rings

## Purpose

This roadmap supplies the algebraic foundations of Clausen–Scholze analytic geometry on which analytic
stacks, six-functor formalisms of solid quasi-coherent sheaves, ring-stack transmutation and the analytic
Habiro ring are built. It starts from Mathlib's light condensed library and ends with:

- analytic rings and their completions;
- idempotent algebras and smashing spectra;
- the solid analytic ring structures on finite-type and general discrete rings;
- discrete Huber pairs and descent over their adic spectra;
- solid Huber rings, bounded rings and Gelfand rings;
- the normed solid base $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$ with its overconvergent function algebras.

The written account followed is J. E. Rodríguez Camargo, *Notes on solid geometry* (arXiv:2603.03012v1), which
expands the Clausen–Scholze lecture series *Analytic Stacks*.

## Scope

In scope:

- Rodríguez Camargo §§2–5 and §§7.1–7.2;
- the solid condensed spectra of Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*, B.6;
- bounded rings, †-nilradicals, uniform completion, Gelfand rings, their Berkovich spectra and the Fredholm
  property from Anschütz–Bosco–Le Bras–Rodríguez Camargo–Scholze (ABLRS, arXiv:2510.15196v2), §§2–3;
- bounded affinoid rings and idempotent algebras from Rodríguez Camargo, *The analytic de Rham stack in rigid
  geometry* (arXiv:2401.07738v1), §§2.4–2.7;
- the explicit normed base of Scholze's course *V5A4 – Habiro cohomology*, Lecture 7: $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$ with
  $|u|=c\in(0,1)$, the overconvergent disc algebras $\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_r$, and algebras obtained by
  forcing prescribed sequences to be null sequences.

Six-functor formalisms and analytic stacks belong to `AnalyticStacks`.

## Conventions

- *Condensed* means *light condensed* throughout. Sites are light profinite sets with finite jointly surjective
  covers (Mathlib `LightProfinite`, `LightCondSet`, `LightCondMod`). The κ-condensed objects of Scholze's 2019
  lecture notes appear only in comparisons of statements.
- $P=\mathbb Z[\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}]/(\infty)$ is the free condensed abelian group on a null sequence, and
  $\mathrm{Null}(A)=\mathrm{Hom}(P,A)$ (RC Definition 3.1.1). Shift is the endomorphism induced by $n\mapsto n+1$.
- An analytic ring is a pair $\mathcal A=(\mathcal A^\triangleright,D(\mathcal A))$ as in RC Definition 4.1.1: a condensed
  animated ring together with its full subcategory of complete modules. $\mathcal A$-modules are complete
  modules. $\operatorname{AnSpec}$ is only introduced in `AnalyticStacks`.
- $R_\square$ denotes the solid analytic ring structure on a discrete ring $R$ (RC Definition 5.4.7), and
  $(R,R^+)_\square$ that of a discrete Huber pair (RC Definition 5.5.4).
- Idempotent algebras are unital maps $1\to A$ with $A\otimes A\simeq A$ (RC Definition 5.1.1). The smashing
  spectrum $\mathrm{Sm}(\mathcal C)$ is the opposite poset of idempotent algebras.
- Norms are nonarchimedean. $\mathbb Z((u))$ is normed by $|u|=c$ with $0<c<1$ fixed.

## Sources

- Rodríguez Camargo, *Notes on solid geometry*, §§2–5, 7.1–7.2.
- Scholze, *Lectures on Condensed Mathematics*, Lectures I–VI, and *Lectures on Analytic Geometry*,
  Lectures II and VII, for the κ-condensed originals.
- Scholze, *Six-Functor Formalisms*, Lecture IX (Definition 9.4, Theorems 9.6–9.10).
- Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*, B.6–B.8.
- ABLRS §§2–3; Rodríguez Camargo, *The analytic de Rham stack in rigid geometry*, §2.
- W. J. G. Ong's notes of Scholze's course *V5A4 – Habiro cohomology* (Bonn, summer 2025), Lecture 7.

## Layers

- **SA.0** Light condensed sets and light condensed abelian groups.
- **SA.1** Solid abelian groups and solid spectra.
- **SA.2** Analytic rings, completions, idempotent algebras and smashing spectra.
- **SA.3** Solid finite-type algebras, discrete Huber pairs and discrete adic spectra.
- **SA.4** Solid Huber rings, bounded and Gelfand rings, and normed solid bases.

## Boundaries

- `EnhancedDerivedSheaves` supplies derived categories of sheaves (E1), adjoint functor theorems and
  localisations (E3), symmetric monoidal ∞-categories (E5:abstract), Ind-completion (E5:presentability) and
  animated rings (E5:animation). `StableHomotopyKTheory` H.5 supplies spectra.
- `AnalyticStacks` owns six-functor formalisms, $\operatorname{AnSpec}$, analytic stacks, Betti stacks,
  cohomological smoothness of solid maps and normed analytic rings as maps to $[0,\infty]^{\mathrm{Betti}}$.
- `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic` TB.0 owns the Berkovich spectrum of a Banach ring. The Tau Ceti
  `AdicSpaces` roadmap owns Huber rings, valuation spectra and rational subsets.
- `VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories` VS2 owns the κ-condensed solid formalism of Fargues–Scholze Chapter VII on
  small v-stacks. This roadmap asserts no comparison between light and κ-condensed solid categories beyond the
  explicit statements for free objects $\mathbb Z_\square[S]$.
- `HabiroRings` HR.2 consumes the solid spectra of SA.1 for Wagner's Lemma B.8.

## Non-goals

Liquid and gaseous analytic ring structures on $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb C$, and the archimedean theory, are not
built here. Neither are the ultrasolid structure $\mathbb Q^{u}_\square$ or the presentability of the ∞-category of
analytic rings: RC's footnote records that the latter is claimed but not proved in the literature, and the
constructions here do not use it.

stages.title: Light condensed sets and light condensed abelian groups
stages.description:
Light condensed sets and light condensed abelian groups (RC §2; Scholze, *Lectures on Condensed Mathematics*,
Lectures I–III).

**Targets.**
- *Light profinite sets.* The equivalent characterisations: metrizable; countable cofiltered limit of finite
  sets (RC Definition 2.1.3 with Proposition 2.1.2). Mathlib's `LightProfinite` and the sequence
  $\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$. For a light profinite $S$, $C(S,\mathbb Z)$ is a free abelian group (RC Proposition 2.1.7).
- *Light condensed sets.* Sheaves for finite jointly surjective families (RC Definition 2.2.1; Mathlib
  `LightCondSet`). Condensation of topological spaces (Mathlib `topCatToLightCondSet`), fully faithful on
  metrizably compactly generated spaces. Quasicompact and quasiseparated condensed sets, and the description of
  quasiseparated condensed sets as injective ind-objects of light compact Hausdorff spaces (RC Definition 2.2.6
  and the proposition following it). Light condensed objects of an ∞-category with countable limits (RC
  Definition 4.0.1), in particular light condensed anima and light condensed spectra.
- *Light condensed abelian groups* (RC Definition 2.3.1; Mathlib `LightCondAb`, `LightCondMod`). RC
  Theorem 2.3.3: Grothendieck abelian with a closed symmetric monoidal structure; countable products exact
  (countable AB4*) and countable AB6; sequential limits of surjections surjective; $\mathbb Z[\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}]$
  internally projective. RC Remark 2.3.4: there is no splitting at the level of light profinite sets.
- *Derived category.* The unbounded derived ∞-category $D(\mathrm{CondAb})$ with its t-structure, derived tensor
  product and internal Hom, identified with light condensed objects of $D(\mathbb Z)$. Also discrete objects, the
  underlying-group functor $M\mapsto M(*)$ and the free objects $\mathbb Z[S]$.
- *Cohomology.* $R\Gamma(T,M)$ for discrete $M$ (RC Definition 2.3.6). For $S$ light profinite,
  $H^0(S,M)=C(S,M)$ and $H^i(S,M)=0$ for $i>0$ (RC Proposition 2.3.7). For light compact Hausdorff $X$,
  condensed cohomology agrees with sheaf cohomology (RC Proposition 2.3.8).

**Inputs.** Mathlib: `LightProfinite`, `LightCondSet`, `LightCondMod`, `LightCondAb`, their free–forgetful
adjunction, monoidal closed structure, `CountableAB4Star` and `IsGrothendieckAbelian` instances, the
epimorphism criteria, and internal projectivity of the free object on $\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$. From
`EnhancedDerivedSheaves`: E1 for derived sheaf categories and presentability; E5:abstract and
E5:presentability for symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories.

**Acceptance.** $\mathbb R/\mathbb R^\delta$ is nonzero, with $(\mathbb R/\mathbb R^\delta)(S)=C(S,\mathbb R)/C^{lc}(S,\mathbb R)$.
$H^*(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\},\mathbb Z)$ is concentrated in degree $0$. The map
$(2\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\})\sqcup(2\mathbb N+1\cup\{\infty\})\to\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ has no section, yet its image under
$\mathbb Z[-]$ splits internally.

stages.title: Solid abelian groups and solid spectra
stages.description:
Solid abelian groups and solid spectra (RC §3; Scholze, *Lectures on Condensed Mathematics*, Lectures V–VI,
and *Lectures on Analytic Geometry*, Lecture II; Wagner, *q-Hodge complexes over the Habiro ring*, B.6–B.8).

**Targets.**
- *Null sequences.* $P$, $\mathrm{Null}(A)$ and summability (RC Definition 3.1.1, Example 3.1.2), and light
  locally profinite sets (RC Definition 3.1.5).
- *Solidity* (RC Definition 3.2.1). $A$ is solid if
  $1-\mathrm{Shift}^*:\mathrm{Hom}(P,A)\to\mathrm{Hom}(P,A)$ is an isomorphism, and $C\in D(\mathrm{CondAb})$ is solid if the
  same holds for $R\mathrm{Hom}$. RC Theorem 2.3.3 shows $P$ is internally projective, which the definition uses
  (Remark 3.2.2).
- *Structure theorem* (RC Theorem 3.2.4 with Proposition 3.2.5). $\mathrm{Solid}$ is a Grothendieck abelian
  subcategory of $\mathrm{CondAb}$ closed under limits, colimits and extensions. It contains $\mathbb Z$ and has a
  solidification left adjoint $(-)^\square$, and a unique symmetric monoidal structure $\otimes^\square$ makes
  $(-)^\square$ symmetric monoidal. $\mathbb R^\square=0$. The derived statements hold for
  $D(\mathrm{CondAb})_\square$.
- *Free solid objects* (RC Theorem 3.3.1). For $S=\lim S_n$, $\mathbb Z[S]^{L\square}\simeq\lim_n\mathbb Z[S_n]$.
  $\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z$ is a compact projective generator of $\mathrm{Solid}$,
  $D(\mathrm{Solid})\simeq D(\mathrm{CondAb})_\square$, and $(-)^{L\square}$ is the left derived functor of $(-)^\square$.
- *Finitely presented solid groups* (RC Theorem 3.4.2, Corollary 3.4.3).
  $\mathrm{Solid}=\mathrm{Ind}(\mathrm{Solid}^{\mathrm{fp}})$. Every finitely presented object has a resolution
  $0\to\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z\to\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z\to M\to0$. $\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z$ is flat for $\otimes^\square$.
- *Computations* (RC §3.5).
  $\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z\otimes^\square\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z=\prod_{\mathbb N\times\mathbb N}\mathbb Z$,
  $\mathbb Z[[T]]\otimes^\square\mathbb Z[[S]]=\mathbb Z[[T,S]]$, and the solid tensor products of $\mathbb Z_p$ and $\mathbb Q_p$.
- *Solid condensed spectra* (Wagner B.6). $\mathrm{Null}=\mathrm{cofib}(\mathbb S[\{\infty\}]\to\mathbb S[\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}])$
  with shift $\sigma$. $M$ is solid if $1-\sigma^*$ is an equivalence on $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{Null},M)$. This defines
  $\mathrm{Sp}_\blacksquare\subseteq\mathrm{Cond}(\mathrm{Sp})$ with solidification and the solid tensor product, and
  $\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb S\otimes^\blacksquare\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb S\simeq\prod_{\mathbb N\times\mathbb N}\mathbb S$. The
  $p$-complete statement used by Wagner Lemma B.8: the solid tensor product preserves bounded below $p$-complete
  objects.

**Inputs.** SA.0. From `StableHomotopyKTheory` H.5:spectra: spectra and $\mathbb S$.

**Acceptance.** $\mathbb Z_p$, $\prod_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z$ and every discrete group are solid. $\mathbb R$ is not solid
and $\mathbb R^\square=0$. $\mathrm{Null}(\mathbb Z_p)$ is the group of sequences tending to $0$. Mathlib's κ-condensed
`CondensedMod.IsSolid`, whose documentation restricts its correctness to $\mathbb Z$-coefficients, is compared with
this notion on the free objects $\mathbb Z[S]$ only.

stages.title: Analytic rings, completions, idempotent algebras and smashing spectra
stages.description:
Analytic rings, completions, idempotent algebras and smashing spectra (RC §4 and §5.1; Scholze,
*Six-Functor Formalisms*, Lecture IX, Definition 9.4).

**Targets.**
- *Analytic rings* (RC Definition 4.1.1, Remark 4.1.2). An uncompleted analytic ring is a condensed animated
  ring $\mathcal A^\triangleright$ with a full subcategory $D(\mathcal A)\subseteq D(\mathcal A^\triangleright)$ that is closed under
  limits and colimits, is $D(\mathrm{CondAb})$-linear, and whose left adjoint preserves connectivity. Analytic rings
  are those with $\mathcal A^\triangleright$ complete. Compare with Scholze Definition 9.4.
- *Completion and colimits* (RC Theorem 4.1.13). The completion functor, left adjoint to the inclusion into
  uncompleted analytic rings. Small colimits of analytic rings. Tensor products
  $D(\mathcal B)\otimes_{D(\mathcal A)}D(\mathcal C)=D(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal C)$.
- *Animation* (RC §4.2, Definitions 4.2.1, 4.2.3). Analytic animated rings obtained from compactly projectively
  generated 1-categories and symmetric functors.
- *Frobenius* (RC Theorem 4.3.2). $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A/p$ is a map of analytic rings.
- *Invariance* (RC Theorem 4.4.1). Analytic ring structures on $\mathcal A^\triangleright$ correspond to suitable abelian
  subcategories of the heart.
- *Morphisms* (RC §4.5). The criterion for a map of condensed rings to underlie a map of analytic rings
  (RC Proposition 4.5.1).
- *Killing algebras* (RC §4.6). Localisation of an analytic ring by killing a compact or idempotent algebra,
  with the induced analytic ring structure.
- *Idempotent algebras and smashing spectra* (RC §5.1). Idempotent algebras in a presentably symmetric monoidal
  stable ∞-category (Definition 5.1.1). The locale $\mathrm{Sm}(\mathcal C)$, with intersections, inclusions and unions
  of closed subsets computed by $\otimes$, absorption and fibre products (Proposition 5.1.2). Open and closed
  immersions in $\mathrm{Affine}(\mathrm{Pr}^L_{st})$ (Definition 5.1.3, Proposition 5.1.4). The Grothendieck topology
  of open localisations with descent for $\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathrm{Pr}^L_{st})$ (Theorem 5.1.6) and its closed-cover variant
  (Remark 5.1.7). Distributive lattices and Stone duality for spectral spaces (Definitions 5.1.8, 5.1.11,
  Theorem 5.1.13, Example 5.1.15).

**Inputs.** SA.1. From `EnhancedDerivedSheaves`: E3 (adjoint functor theorem, accessible localisations),
E5:presentability (presentable categories, Ind-completion) and E5:animation (animated rings).

**Acceptance.** $\mathbb Z_\square$ (solid abelian groups) is an analytic ring. Every condensed animated ring with all
its condensed modules is an analytic ring (the trivial structure). $\mathbb Z_\square\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z_\square\simeq\mathbb Z_\square$
as analytic rings. The idempotent algebras $\mathbb Z[1/p]$ and $\mathbb Z_p$ of $D(\mathbb Z_\square)$ satisfy
$\mathbb Z[1/p]\otimes^\square\mathbb Z_p\simeq\mathbb Q_p$.

stages.title: Solid finite-type algebras, discrete Huber pairs and discrete adic spectra
stages.description:
Solid finite-type algebras, discrete Huber pairs and discrete adic spectra (RC §§5.2–5.6; Scholze,
*Six-Functor Formalisms*, Theorems 9.6–9.10, 9.15, first part).

**Targets.**
- *$\mathbb Z[T]_\square$* (RC §5.2). $T$-solid modules (Definition 5.2.1). $D(\mathbb Z[T]_\square)$ as a localisation of
  $D((\mathbb Z[T],\mathbb Z)_\square)$ (Proposition 5.2.2). $\mathbb Z[T]_\square$ is an analytic ring with
  $\mathbb Z[T]_\square[S]=\lim_n\mathbb Z[T][S_n]$ (Theorem 5.2.3).
- *Finite-type algebras* (RC §5.3). $r$-solid modules (Definition 5.3.1). Theorem 5.3.2: for $R$ of finite type
  over $\mathbb Z$, $R_\square[S]=\lim_nR[S_n]$, $D(R_\square)$ is the derived category of its heart, and
  $\prod_{\mathbb N}R$ is flat. Propositions 5.3.3, 5.3.7 and 5.3.12 (complete modules for finitely generated
  ideals). Scholze Theorem 9.6 for almost finitely presented animated $\mathbb Z$-algebras.
- *Schemes* (RC §5.4). The fully faithful embedding $R\mapsto R^{\mathrm{cond}}$ of rings as analytic rings with the
  trivial structure (Proposition 5.4.1) and Zariski covers (Propositions 5.4.3, 5.4.6). $R_\square$ for arbitrary rings as a colimit over finite-type subalgebras (Definition 5.4.7, Remark 5.4.8).
  $(-)_\square:\mathrm{Ring}\to\mathrm{AnRing}$ is fully faithful and colimit-preserving (Proposition 5.4.11).
  Principal opens (Proposition 5.4.15). Zariski covers of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ give open covers of
  $\mathrm{Sm}(D(R_\square))$ (Theorem 5.4.16).
- *Discrete Huber pairs* (RC §5.5). Animated discrete Huber pairs (Definition 5.5.1) and their compact
  generators (Lemma 5.5.2). The pre-analytic and analytic structures $(A,S)_\square$ (Definition 5.5.4), which
  depend only on the integral closure (Scholze Theorem 9.8). The functor
  $(R,R^+)\mapsto(R,R^+)_\square$ is fully faithful and colimit-preserving (RC Proposition 5.5.6; Scholze
  Theorem 9.10), with the warning of Scholze 9.11 on free modules outside finite type.
- *Discrete adic spectra* (RC §5.6). $\operatorname{Spa}(R,R^+)$ for discrete Huber pairs (Definition 5.6.1) and the
  bijection of Proposition 5.6.3. Rational localisations are idempotent algebras (Proposition 5.6.4).
  Structure presheaves (Definition 5.6.5, Proposition 5.6.6). Theorem 5.6.8:
  $U\mapsto D((\mathcal O_X(U),\mathcal O_X(U)^+)_\square)$ is a sheaf on finite disjoint unions of rational subsets,
  with values in presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories; this is the descent part of Scholze
  Theorem 9.15. The modified adic spectrum $\operatorname{Spa}(R,R^+)^{\mathrm{mod}}$ and its spectrality (Definition 5.6.9,
  Lemma 5.6.10).

**Inputs.** SA.2. From `SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.0: schemes and Zariski covers. From Tau Ceti
`AdicSpaces` Layers 1–2: valuation spectra, $\operatorname{Spa}$ and rational subsets, applied to discrete Huber rings.

**Acceptance.** $\mathbb Z[T]_\square[*]=\mathbb Z[T]$ and $\mathbb Z[T]_\square[\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}]$ are computed. The
pairs $(\mathbb Z[T],\mathbb Z)$ and $(\mathbb Z[T],\mathbb Z[T])$ give different analytic rings: a complete
$(\mathbb Z[T],\mathbb Z)_\square$-module $M$ is $T$-solid exactly when $R\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb Z((T^{-1})),M)=0$ (proof of
Proposition 5.2.2). The rational cover of $\operatorname{Spa}(\mathbb Z[T],\mathbb Z[T])$ by
$\{|T|\le1\}$ and $\{|T|\ge1\}$ satisfies descent.

stages.title: Solid Huber rings, bounded and Gelfand rings, and normed solid bases
stages.description:
Solid Huber rings, bounded and Gelfand rings, and normed solid bases (RC §§7.1–7.2; RC, *The analytic de Rham
stack in rigid geometry*, §§2.4–2.7; ABLRS §§2–3; V5A4 Lecture 7).

**Targets.**
- *Solid Huber rings* (RC §7.1). Solid pre-analytic Huber pairs and $(\mathcal A^\triangleright,S)_\square$
  (Definition 7.1.1). Examples 7.1.4 relating discrete Huber pairs. The right adjoint of
  Proposition 7.1.5. The anima of topologically nilpotent elements (Definition 7.1.6, Remark 7.1.8). Solid Tate
  algebras $\mathcal A[T_1,\dots,T_n]_\square$ (Definition 7.1.9, Example 7.1.10).
- *Rational localisations and the solid spectrum* (RC §7.2). Standard rational localisations
  (Definition 7.2.1). The solid spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}^\square(\mathcal A)$, obtained by Stone duality from the lattice
  generated by rational localisations (Definition 7.2.7), and its properties (Proposition 7.2.12).
- *Bounded rings* (RC 2401.07738 §§2.4–2.6; ABLRS §2). Idempotent algebras of rigid geometry; the condensed
  nilradical; bounded affinoid rings. For a bounded $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra $A$: the subring $A^{\le1}$ and the rings
  $\mathbb Q_{p,\square}\langle\mathbb N[S]\rangle_{\le r}$ (ABLRS Definitions 2.2.3, 2.2.7, 2.2.8); †-reduction and the
  pullback square of Proposition 2.2.20 (Definition 2.2.19); uniform completion $A^u$ (Definition 2.3.1,
  Proposition 2.3.6). RC 2401.07738 Proposition 2.6.16(3) is replaced by the ABLRS treatment (ABLRS footnote to
  Remark 2.3.5).
- *Gelfand rings* (ABLRS §3). Gelfand $\mathbb Q_p$-algebras (Definition 3.1.1), stable under colimits
  (Proposition 3.1.4). The Berkovich spectrum $\mathcal M(A)$ via $A^u$ (Definition 3.1.5) and its closed subsets
  (Proposition 3.1.9). Residue fields (Definition 3.1.15). The functor to sheaves on $\mathcal M(A)$
  (Proposition 3.1.16) and the map to the Berkovich spectrum (§3.2: Proposition 3.2.5, Definition 3.2.8,
  Propositions 3.2.10–3.2.11). The Fredholm property (Definition 3.3.1, Proposition 3.3.5).
- *The normed base $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$* (V5A4 Example 7.3, Definitions 7.4–7.6).
  - The solid analytic ring $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$ with $|u|=c$.
  - The overconvergent disc algebras
    $\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_r=\{\sum a_nT^n:\exists r'>r,\ |a_n|r'^n\to0\}$ with their solid structure. The
    map $\mathbb Z((u))_\square[T]\to(\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_r)_\square$ is an idempotent algebra.
  - The algebra of entire functions $\{\sum a_nT^n:\forall r,\ |a_n|r^n\to0\}$ as the limit of the disc algebras.
  - For an analytic ring $\mathcal A$ over $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$ and a sequence $(a_n)$ in $\mathcal A^\triangleright(*)$: the
    universal $\mathcal A$-algebra in which $(a_n)$ is a null sequence, and the colimit over $k$ of those in which
    $(a_n/u^{kn})$ is a null sequence (the construction of V5A4 Remark 7.13, modelled on ABLRS
    Definition 2.2.3).

**Inputs.** SA.3. From `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic` TB.0: Berkovich spectra of Banach rings. From Tau
Ceti `AdicSpaces` Layer 0: Huber rings, rings of definition and Tate algebras.

**Acceptance.** $\mathbb Q_p$ and the Tate algebra $\mathbb Q_p\langle T\rangle$ are Gelfand rings. In $\mathbb Z((u))_\square$ every nonzero
integer has norm $1$, so $\mathbb Z((u))$ is not a bounded $\mathbb Q_p$-algebra and the $\mathbb Z((u))$-theory is built separately. The disc algebras
satisfy $\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_r\otimes_{\mathbb Z((u))_\square[T]}\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_{r}\simeq
\mathbb Z((u))\langle T\rangle^\dagger_r$. The sequence $(T^k/u^{k-1})_k$ is a null sequence exactly on the disc of
radius $c$ (V5A4 Example 7.3). The analytic ring obtained by forcing $((q;q)_n)_n$ to decay rapidly receives a
map from $\mathbb Z[q]$ that factors through the $(q;q)_n$-adic completion (compare V5A4 Lemma 7.10).
